name: Project scaffolding and dependencies
description: Set up the project so `main.py` starts a local Flask web server. Add Flask, numpy, scipy, matplotlib, and pytest as dependencies via `uv add` (do not use pip/conda). Create the package layout for the stats engine (e.g. `h2h/stats.py`) separate from the web layer (e.g. `h2h/app.py`), with `main.py` at the repo root simply importing and running the Flask app. Running `uv run main.py` must start the server and serve a placeholder page at `/`.
tests: `uv run main.py` starts without error and binds to a localhost port.
A GET request to `/` returns HTTP 200.
The stats module can be imported independently of Flask (`import h2h.stats` succeeds with Flask not running).

name: Per-arrow score PMF from handicap
description: In the stats engine, implement a function that takes an AGB handicap and an `archeryutils.targets.Target`, and returns the full per-arrow score probability mass function (a mapping of score value to probability), derived from `sigma_r(handicap, distance)` and the target's `face_spec`, using the same ring-probability terms `archeryutils` computes internally for `HandicapScheme.arrow_score`/`_s_bar`. Must not duplicate `archeryutils`'s scoring-system logic beyond what is necessary to expose the per-ring probabilities instead of just their mean.
tests: For a range of handicaps (e.g. 0, 10, 25, 50, 80) and at least two target faces, the PMF's probabilities sum to 1 (within floating point tolerance).
For the same inputs, the PMF's expected value (`sum(score * prob)`) matches `archeryutils`'s `HandicapScheme.arrow_score(handicap, target)` within floating point tolerance.
All PMF probabilities are >= 0.

name: n_pass score distribution via convolution
description: Implement a function that takes a per-arrow PMF (from task 2) and an integer `n_pass`, and returns the exact probability distribution of the summed score over `n_pass` arrows, computed via discrete self-convolution (not Monte Carlo, not a Gaussian/CLT approximation).
tests: For n_pass in {1, 6, 12, 60}, the resulting distribution's probabilities sum to 1 (within floating point tolerance).
The resulting distribution's expected value equals `n_pass * arrow_score(handicap, target)` within floating point tolerance.
For n_pass = 1, the result is identical to the input per-arrow PMF.

name: Percentile computation and pass-winner decision
description: Implement a function that, given an n_pass score distribution (from task 3) and an archer's actual observed pass score, returns that archer's percentile (the probability of scoring at or below the observed score under their own distribution). Implement a second function that takes two archers' percentiles (plus their raw scores, for tie-breaking) and returns the pass winner, using the tie-break rule: equal percentile -> higher raw score wins; still equal -> coin flip.
tests: Percentile values returned are always in [0, 1].
An archer scoring the minimum possible score for their distribution gets a percentile at or near 0; scoring the maximum possible gets a percentile at or near 1.
Given two different percentiles, the winner-decision function picks the higher one.
Given equal percentiles but different raw scores, the winner-decision function picks the higher raw score.

Given equal percentiles and equal raw scores, the winner-decision function still returns a valid winner (does not error or hang) and this is verified as a genuine coin flip (not always the same archer) across repeated calls.

name: Match/round data model and orchestration
description: Implement `Archer`, `Pass`, `Match`, and `Round` data structures per AISpec.md §6. `Round` should source its target/distance/arrow-count metadata from `archeryutils.load_rounds` (default: Portsmouth). `Match` should compute the number of passes as `60 / n_pass` and reject non-divisor `n_pass` values. Provide a function to record a pass's scores for both archers (computing percentiles and pass winner via tasks 2-4) and a function to compute the overall match result (majority of passes wins; even split is a draw) once all passes are recorded.
tests: Creating a `Match` with an `n_pass` that does not divide 60 evenly raises a clear error.
For n_pass = 12, a `Match` has exactly 5 passes.
Recording pass scores for both archers correctly updates the running per-archer pass-win tally.
A match where one archer wins a strict majority of passes reports that archer as the overall winner.
A match with an even pass count and an even split of pass wins reports a draw.

name: Match setup UI (archer entry, pairing, n_pass slider)
description: Build the setup page: form to add archers (name, handicap, optional bowstyle label), automatic sequential pairing into matches, and a slider restricted to the divisors of 60 ({1,2,3,4,5,6,10,12,15,20,30,60}, default 12) to set `n_pass` for the session before scoring starts. Submitting creates the in-memory `Match` objects for the session.
tests: Adding an odd number of archers flags the last one as unpaired and excludes them from scoring, without crashing the app.
The n_pass slider cannot be set to a value that is not a divisor of 60 (UI prevents it, or server-side validation rejects it with a clear error).
Submitting valid archer data creates one Match per pair with the chosen n_pass.

name: Pass score entry and live results (basic mode)
description: Build the basic-mode scoring page: for each match, one input box per archer for the current pass's total score. On submission, display that pass's winner and the running match score (passes won so far by each archer), and progress to the next pass. After the final pass, display the overall match result (winner or draw) per task 5.
tests: Entering both archers' scores for a pass and submitting displays a pass winner consistent with the stats engine's decision (task 4) for those inputs.
The running match score displayed after each pass matches the tally computed by the Match object.
After the final pass of a match, the overall match result shown matches the Match object's computed result.

name: Basic/Advanced UI toggle
description: Add a visible, session-wide toggle switching between basic mode (task 7 only) and advanced mode (task 9). Toggling must not lose any already-entered scores or match progress.
tests: Toggling from basic to advanced mode and back preserves all previously entered pass scores and running results.
The toggle state is visually clear (unambiguous which mode is active).

name: Advanced mode: distribution plots and maths explanation
description: In advanced mode, for each scored pass, render (via matplotlib, as a static image) each archer's handicap-implied n_pass score distribution with their actual score and resulting percentile marked. Also display a short, human-readable explanation of the underlying method (summarising AISpec.md §2: handicap -> sigma_r -> per-arrow PMF -> convolved n_pass distribution -> percentile comparison), including the explicit note that the bowstyle-variance correction is not applied in this version.
tests: For a scored pass, an image is rendered showing both archers' distributions with their observed scores marked.
The maths explanation text is present and mentions that bowstyle-variance correction is not applied.
Advanced-mode content does not appear when the toggle (task 8) is set to basic mode.

name: End-to-end integration check
description: Write an integration test (or documented manual test procedure, if automated browser testing is out of scope) that runs a full session end to end: add archers with differing handicaps, set n_pass, enter all pass scores for a match, and confirm the displayed overall match result matches an independently hand-calculated expectation for at least one concrete worked example (e.g. using the mean-only comparison as a sanity check that the favoured archer's percentile calculation is directionally correct).
tests: A full session (setup through final match result) completes without error for at least 2 archers and one full round of passes.
The final displayed result for the worked example matches the independently computed expectation.
Restarting the app clears all prior match state (confirms no unintended persistence, per Assumption 7).

name: Pass score validation and integer display
description: Per Specification/feedback.md 'Feedback 1': a pass score over n_pass arrows must be a whole number in [0, n_pass * MAX_SCORE_PER_ARROW], with MAX_SCORE_PER_ARROW hard-coded to 10. Reject invalid input (non-integer, negative, above the maximum, or non-numeric) with a specific, human-readable error message instead of a 500 or silent acceptance, without recording anything. Recorded scores must always display as plain integers (no trailing '.0').
tests: A negative score is rejected with a message naming the valid range.
A score above n_pass * 10 is rejected with a message naming the valid range.
A non-integer score (e.g. 100.5) is rejected with a 'whole number' message.
Non-numeric input (e.g. 'abc') is rejected with a clear message, not a 500.
0 and n_pass * 10 (the inclusive boundaries) are accepted.
A recorded score renders without a trailing '.0' in the match page.

name: Per-pass equivalent handicap
description: Add a full-round-equivalent AGB handicap column per archer per pass: the handicap that would, on average, produce that archer's actual pass score, computed via archeryutils's own handicap_from_score rootfinder over a one-off Round built from n_pass arrows at the match's target. Undefined (displayed as '-') for a score of 0.
tests: A nonzero pass score gets a recorded equivalent handicap for both archers.
A zero pass score has an undefined (None) equivalent handicap.
A lower pass score implies a numerically larger (worse) AGB handicap than a higher pass score.
The equivalent-handicap column is visible in the match page's pass table once a pass is scored.

name: Interactive single-graph distribution chart
description: Replace the per-pass static matplotlib PNG charts with one interactive chart per match (Chart.js via a pinned CDN version): both archers' n_pass score distributions as smoothed, shaded curves on one shared graph, trimmed to a sensible x-range (not the full achievable score range) rather than two separate discretised bar charts. Hovering shows both archers' current probability values at that score. Each scored pass's actual scores are marked as vertical lines; only the most recent pass's markers are shown by default, with a checkbox to reveal every previous pass's markers too.
tests: h2h.chart_data.build_match_chart_data returns a payload with both archers' distribution points, a shared x_min/x_max range narrower than the full 0..n_pass*10 range for two differently-skilled archers, and a y_max ceiling.
The x-range still gets a sensible minimum width for a near-zero-variance distribution (e.g. two handicap-0 archers), even though its mean sits at the edge of the achievable range.
Every distribution point falls within the reported x-range.
Scored passes appear in the payload in order with their raw scores; no scored passes gives an empty list.
The match page in advanced mode renders a canvas#match-chart, embeds the chart payload as window.MATCH_CHART_DATA, and does not render either in basic mode.

UPDATE: subsequently verified in a real headless-Edge browser (via an ephemeral Selenium install) during Feedback 2 processing -- confirmed the chart renders two curve datasets, the checkbox correctly adds/removes prior passes' marker datasets (verified via Chart.js's own dataset list and a screenshot), and no JS console errors occur (aside from an unrelated favicon 404).

name: Subscript typesetting for underscore identifiers
description: Any underscore-separated identifier shown in user-facing text (n_pass, sigma_r) must be typeset with a proper subscript (n<sub>pass</sub>, sigma<sub>r</sub>) instead of displaying the literal underscore. Error messages that would otherwise need to show such an identifier are reworded to avoid it instead, since plain-text error strings can't carry markup.
tests: The setup page renders 'n<sub>pass</sub>' and not a literal 'n_pass' label.
No user-facing template text contains a literal 'n_pass' or 'sigma_r' outside of Jinja value expressions (verified by grep across h2h/templates).
The invalid-n_pass error message is reworded to avoid the raw identifier.

name: Round-robin rotation scheduler
description: Add h2h/rotation.py: a Flask- and stats-independent module generating a round-robin ('circle method') rotation schedule over n_archers positions (0..n_archers-1) for a requested number of rotations. Odd n_archers gets a bye slot each rotation (one archer index with no opponent that rotation). If requested rotations < a full round-robin's length, truncate; if more, cycle the schedule from the start to fill the rest (Specification/AISpec.md Assumption 13).
tests: For even n_archers, a full-length schedule has every archer paired with every other archer exactly once across n_archers-1 rotations, and no archer has a bye.
For odd n_archers, a full-length schedule has n_archers rotations, each with exactly one archer on the bye, and every archer has exactly one bye across the full schedule.
No rotation pairs an archer with themselves, and no archer appears twice (as two different opponents) within the same rotation.
Requesting fewer rotations than a full round-robin needs returns a truncated prefix of the full schedule.
Requesting more rotations than a full round-robin needs repeats the schedule from the start for the extra rotations.
n_archers=2 produces a single rotation with one pair and no bye.

name: Per-archer target resolution (round mode x bowstyle)
description: Add a function resolving an archer's effective archeryutils Target from the event's round mode (indoor+Portsmouth/WA18, or outdoor) and the archer's bowstyle, per Specification/AISpec.md section 5.2a: indoor Compound uses the *_compound scoring-system variant (portsmouth_compound / wa18_compound) of the same face/distance; indoor Recurve/Barebow use the plain variant; outdoor uses one single fixed target (AISpec.md Assumption 12: wa720_70's target) for every bowstyle.
tests: Indoor Portsmouth + Compound resolves to portsmouth_compound's target (same diameter/distance as portsmouth, scoring_system '10_zone_compound').
Indoor Portsmouth + Recurve or Barebow resolves to portsmouth's own target ('10_zone').
Indoor WA18 + Compound resolves to wa18_compound's target; + Recurve/Barebow resolves to wa18's target.
Outdoor mode resolves to the same fixed target regardless of bowstyle (Recurve, Compound, and Barebow all get an identical Target).
The resolved target's `indoor` flag is correct in each case (True for both indoor rounds, False for outdoor), so per_arrow_pmf's automatic arrow-diameter selection is unaffected.

name: Event data model (replaces fixed-pair Match)
description: Add h2h.models.Event, Rotation, and result-tracking structures per Specification/AISpec.md section 6, replacing the old single-pair Match for new code (existing Match-based tests/routes are migrated in later tasks, not kept alongside). Event holds archers, total_arrows, n_pass, round_mode, the rotation schedule (task 15), and each archer's own precomputed n_pass score distribution (handicap + task-16-resolved target, independent of opponent). Provides recording a rotation's scores (validating each score per the existing MAX_SCORE_PER_ARROW rule), computing each archer's percentile/equivalent handicap for that pass, deciding each pair's pass winner, and maintaining a running pairwise result (win/loss/draw) per pair of archers who have shared at least one rotation.
tests: Constructing an Event with n_archers/total_arrows/n_pass computes a schedule of total_arrows // n_pass rotations via task 15.
Recording a rotation's scores for all its pairs (and bye archer, if any) computes each participant's percentile and equivalent handicap using their OWN resolved target/distribution, not a shared one.
A bye archer's pass is recorded (score + percentile) but produces no winner and does not appear in any pairwise result.
After a pair shares one pass, querying that pair's pairwise result returns a win/loss based on that pass's winner.
If a pair shares multiple passes (schedule cycling, task 15), their pairwise result aggregates across all shared passes (majority; even split is a draw), mirroring the old Match.result() semantics.
Invalid scores (non-integer, out of range) are rejected via the same validation as before, leaving the rotation unrecorded.
Two archers with different bowstyles under indoor mode get correctly different target-based distributions (task 16 wired through).

name: Stage 1 setup UI (event configuration)
description: Build the Stage 1 page per Specification/AISpec.md section 5.1: n_archers (integer, >=2), total_arrows (default 60), n_pass (snap control restricted to divisors of the CHOSEN total_arrows, not a fixed set), round mode (indoor -> Portsmouth/WA18 sub-choice, or outdoor). Submitting validates inputs, builds the rotation schedule (task 15) over n_archers positions, stores it in session state, and proceeds to Stage 2 (task 19) with exactly n_archers archer-detail rows expected.
tests: Submitting valid Stage 1 inputs stores a schedule with the correct number of rotations and redirects to Stage 2.
n_pass values that don't divide the chosen total_arrows are rejected server-side with a clear error, re-rendering Stage 1 without crashing.
Changing total_arrows changes which n_pass values are offered/accepted (e.g. total_arrows=40 accepts n_pass=8 but not n_pass=12).
n_archers < 2 is rejected with a clear error.
Selecting indoor requires (and outdoor omits) the Portsmouth/WA18 sub-choice in the submitted form.

name: Stage 2 setup UI (archer details)
description: Build the Stage 2 page per Specification/AISpec.md section 5.2: exactly n_archers rows (from Stage 1, not a generic fixed count) collecting name, bowstyle (dropdown: Recurve/Compound/Barebow, required), and handicap. Submitting binds these Archers to the Stage 1 schedule's positions in entry order and constructs the Event (task 17), then proceeds to the rotation-scoring view (task 20).
tests: Stage 2 renders exactly n_archers rows, matching whatever n_archers was chosen in Stage 1.
Submitting valid archer details for all rows creates an Event and redirects to the rotation-scoring view.
A missing or invalid bowstyle value is rejected with a clear error (dropdown only offers the three valid values).
Attempting to reach Stage 2 without having completed Stage 1 redirects back to Stage 1 instead of erroring.

name: Rotation scoring UI
description: Build the per-rotation scoring page per Specification/AISpec.md section 5.3: for the event's current (first not-fully-scored) rotation, show one score-entry box per archer in each pair (grouped by pair) plus a single box for the bye archer's score if there is one that rotation. Submitting records all of that rotation's scores via Event (task 17) in one action and advances to the next rotation (or shows event-complete state once every rotation is scored).
tests: The scoring page for a rotation shows exactly the right set of input boxes: one pair per matched pair, plus the bye archer's single box if n_archers is odd that rotation.
Submitting a rotation's scores for all pairs (and bye, if present) records them and advances next_pass_index()-equivalent to the following rotation.
An invalid score anywhere in the submitted rotation is rejected with a specific error and does not partially record the rotation.
After the final rotation is scored, the page indicates the event is complete rather than prompting for another rotation.

name: Per-pass and pairwise results display
description: Display both result levels from Specification/AISpec.md section 5.4: a per-rotation table of every scored pass (score/percentile/equivalent handicap per archer, winner if paired), and a pairwise-results view listing every pair of archers who have shared at least one rotation with their aggregated win/loss/draw -- explicitly NOT a ranked leaderboard across all archers (out of scope).
tests: After scoring a rotation, the per-pass table shows that rotation's results for every participant, matching the Event object's recorded PassResults.
The pairwise-results view shows an entry for every pair that has shared a rotation so far, with the correct win/loss/draw, and no entry for pairs that haven't met yet.
The pairwise-results view does not compute or display any single ranked score/points total across all archers.

name: Static handicap conversion tool
description: Add a standalone page/route per Specification/AISpec.md section 5.5: pick Portsmouth or WA18, enter a full-round score, see the resulting AGB handicap to 1 decimal place, computed via archeryutils's real Portsmouth/WA18 Round objects (not a synthetic partial round). Reachable from Stage 2 and independently from the nav at any time; its result is never stored against any archer or wired into the event.
tests: Submitting a valid Portsmouth score returns the correct handicap to 1 decimal place, matching archeryutils.handicaps.handicap_scheme('AGB').handicap_from_score directly on the real Portsmouth round.
Submitting a valid WA18 score returns the correct handicap similarly against the real WA18 round.
An out-of-range or non-numeric score shows a friendly error instead of a 500.
The tool is reachable from the nav independent of where the scorer currently is in event setup/scoring.

name: Adapt advanced-mode charts to per-pair-with-shared-history
description: Update h2h/chart_data.py and the advanced-mode UI to build a distribution chart for each pair of archers who have shared at least one rotation (per Specification/AISpec.md section 5.6), rather than one fixed match's two archers. Each archer's distribution now comes from their own resolved target (task 16), not a shared match target. Preserve the existing behaviour verified for Feedback 1: trimmed x-range, shared y-axis, only-latest-pass markers by default with a checkbox for all shared passes.
tests: build_match_chart_data (or its Event-based equivalent) produces a valid payload for any pair that has shared at least one rotation, using each archer's own distribution.
Two archers with different resolved targets (e.g. different bowstyles indoors) get visibly different distribution curves in the payload.
No chart payload/canvas is generated for a pair that hasn't shared a rotation yet.
Re-verify in a real browser (per the working method established for task 13) that the checkbox still correctly toggles prior shared passes' markers under the new per-pair data source.

name: Retire the old fixed-pair setup/scoring routes and migrate tests
description: Remove the old single-stage setup page and fixed-pair Match-based routes/templates now superseded by tasks 18-21, and update/replace the existing test suite (tests/test_app.py, tests/test_models.py, tests/test_integration.py, tests/test_chart_data.py) to exercise the new two-stage, rotation-based flow instead. Do not leave dead/unreachable old routes or templates behind.
tests: No route still references the old single-pair Match model or the old one-stage setup form.
The full test suite passes with no references to the removed Match-based routes/behaviour.
Grep confirms no leftover dead template files or unused imports from the old flow.

name: End-to-end integration check for the rotation flow
description: Write an integration test exercising the full new flow end to end: Stage 1 -> Stage 2 -> score every rotation -> confirm per-pass and pairwise results are correct, for both an even and an odd n_archers case (covering bye handling), and for both indoor (with mixed bowstyles) and outdoor round modes.
tests: Even n_archers: full event completes, every archer's pairwise results match the expected round-robin coverage (everyone faces everyone once, given enough rotations).
Odd n_archers: each rotation has exactly one bye archer whose pass is recorded with no winner, and byes are distributed as the scheduler intends.

Indoor mode with a mix of Compound and Recurve/Barebow archers: verify (via h2h.stats/h2h.models directly, as an independent check) that the Compound archer's recorded equivalent handicap/percentile used the compound-scoring target, not the plain one.
Outdoor mode: all archers use the same fixed target regardless of bowstyle.
Restarting the app (fresh SessionState) clears all event state, consistent with Assumption 7.
